metadata.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
metadata.status: Accepted alternative-story plan; vendor contracts, measured demonstration performance and unspecified operating details remain execution gates.

positioning.tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning.audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.
positioning.partner_message: Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.

schedule.activity: Newspaper and business-press teasers introduce Aurelia and the personal-assistant promise; coming this spring, followed by June 5 launch date; brochure and invitation requests.
Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
Press previews, dealer/staff preparation, launch invitations, television-station outreach and complete venue rehearsal.
NCC premiere in Anaheim, five-city Academy announcement, package and availability presentation, registration and ordering.
Technical sessions, repeated hands-on demonstrations, professional recording of every Logix NCC presentation and Academy registration.

Edit and freely distribute television packages; run Academy courses and dealer demonstrations; advertise practical business uses, real package prices, local dates and documented customer experience as it becomes available.

Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.

Begin BPI dealer qualification and accountant demonstration access, permission-based case studies and defined paid setup assistance. Each initial Academy centre has access to a BPI specialist; recruit or train ahead of demand.

Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent.

Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.

television_commercial.format: Proposed 60-second film-trailer-style advertisement; final 10–15 seconds show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, logo and June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable BPI report with its own branding; detailed accounting explanation belongs in print and follow-up films.
television_commercial.casting_status: Fictional casting proposal; availability, fee and contract not established.
television_commercial.story: Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration.
television_commercial.tone: Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence.
television_commercial.conversion: Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.

premiere.venue: Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.

stages.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.
Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.
Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.
Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The following BPI demonstration shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in the subsequent partners section.

Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with Adam investment and AION/Logix cooperation disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice, 50% tuition purchase credit and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates and exact tuition once finalised. BPI-authorised courses start June 12; specialist support is provided by BPI.

State complete package contents and prices, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training/setup prices.

premiere.display: Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

technical_sessions.topic: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem
technical_sessions.content: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation/licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development.

technical_sessions.topic: Aurelia C compiler Integrated Development Environment and SDK
technical_sessions.content: Build and run an application, common TUI behaviour, published interfaces and C source portability without promising universal binary compatibility.

academy.tuition_positioning: A modest fraction of an Aurelia package price; publish exact tuition and a named package comparison when commercial prices are selected. Generated pricing proposals are not approved tuition.
academy.teaching: Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases.

credit.dealer_reimbursement: Logix reimburses participating dealers; do not deduct the credit from their agreed margin.
credit.scope: Standalone two-day Fundamentals. Existing $150 vouchers for the other before-you-buy courses remain unchanged; no stacking or extension to other courses is implied.
credit.accounting: Reserve the redeemed credit once as promotional expense across the course and computer sale, outside recurring manufacturing costs.

academy.sales: Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.
academy.bpi_support: Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate; no automatic Fundamentals credit for BPI courses.

broadcast_program.scope: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions.
broadcast_program.production: Professional multi-camera crew with clean presenter audio, audience/reaction coverage and close-ups of the computer, screen, connections and printouts. Retain full-session recordings and production masters.
deliverables: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage
broadcast_program.distribution: Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.
broadcast_program.editorial_policy: Station participation, scheduling and editorial selection are voluntary; no guaranteed airtime, compulsory advertising purchase or claimed editorial endorsement. Identify the material as supplied by Logix.
broadcast_program.rights: Arrange presenter, partner, music and production rights covering free television redistribution before recording. Michael Douglas commercial footage may be included only if separately cleared for this use.
broadcast_program.fidelity: Do not accelerate startup or recalculation, conceal failures through misleading cuts, or present pre-recorded footage as a live result. Identify edited excerpts and show only qualified claims.
broadcast_program.timing: Record throughout June 5–8; begin station outreach before NCC and distribute edited packages after the conference as edits and broadcast clearances are completed. Exact delivery dates and runtime remain production decisions.
broadcast_program.engineering: Qualify a custom Aurelia digital-video-to-projection/recording path; rehearse readability, lighting and sound in the hired room. Use a backup demonstration system and clearly identified recorded fallback.

acceptance_gates: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, tuition, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified and separately quoted.
Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

business_sessions.topic: Setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage
business_sessions.date_window: 1978-06-05 to 1978-06-08; session time to be booked

commercial_configurations.policy: Dealer component baskets using separately licensed BPI products; no new fixed-price SKU or second contribution reduction. Prices calculated in pricing_results.json. Training/setup, tax and unqualified extra hardware excluded.

cost_boundary.classification: Marketing and sales-program expenditure separate from unit manufacturing and recurring course delivery.
cost_items: Venue, projection conversion, audio, rehearsal and professional recording crew
Editing, music/rights, broadcast masters, station copies and dispatch
Press material, enquiry handling and dealer preparation
Academy launch fit-out, demonstration stock and registration setup
Fundamentals purchase-credit exposure and dealer reimbursement
BPI pilot, export/import development, specialist staffing, dealer qualification and case-study production; amounts unbudgeted, not zero
BPI module-upgrade credits and incremental support; independently accounted, not Logix hardware manufacturing cost
cost_boundary.treatment: No fabricated campaign total and no automatic per-unit allocation. Reuse existing recurring course costs; do not charge Academy teaching twice. Free station supply creates no content-license revenue; reach and uptake are not guaranteed.

metadata.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
metadata.status: Accepted alternative-story programme; dates are scenario choices, adoption counts are targets, measurements and unsigned commercial agreements remain open.

positioning.message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
positioning.objective: Expand independent CP/M application compatibility and FlexiBUS peripheral adoption across competing vendors; video is optional. Ecosystem success can include lost Aurelia share.
positioning.openness: Documented interfaces, non-exclusive implementation rights and predictable commercial access; CP/M remains commercially licensed, not automatically free or open-source.

profiles.name: CP/M application compatibility
profiles.required: Named OS core version, optional extension version, ISA, TPA/resource budget, adapters and qualified application editions; common document formats and documented APIs.
profiles.optional: FlexiBUS and Logix video; native host display, disks and conventional ports remain valid.
profiles.limits: Standard CP/M availability does not guarantee every extended application, Z80-only binary, file system or floppy format.

profiles.name: FlexiBUS peripheral compatibility
profiles.required: Published electrical/transport rules plus device-class profile, host driver, diagnostics and named qualification.
profiles.optional: CP/M and Logix video; other OS/CPU hosts can implement their own drivers.
profiles.limits: Identification is not feature compatibility. V1 is one device per point-to-point host port, no implied passive hub or daisy chain; faster rate permits at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

profiles.name: Logix display compatibility
profiles.required: Distinguish software API conformance from optional controller/card, digital link and qualified monitor modes.
profiles.optional: FlexiBUS and adoption of the full Aurelia architecture.
profiles.limits: 80-column display requires a qualified 640-pixel monitor; existing 320-pixel launch monitors do not gain it from a card alone.

governance.participants: Independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers; prospective membership is not a signed agreement.
commitments: Published specifications, versioning and backward-support policy
Reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process
Non-exclusive implementation rights, own-brand products and published access terms
Equal access to qualified components and disclosed supply priorities
Manufacturer representation in a compatibility working group
open_terms: Final licence/royalty terms and reference-code redistribution rights
Support duration, staffing and legacy maintenance budget
Working-group charter, voting and certification operator
Certification fees, supply allocations, lead times and warranties

schedule.activity: Begin confidential briefings and engineering-kit evaluations. Prioritise North Star and Vector Graphic as prospects; approach Cromemco, Altos, Intertec and Heath selectively. Invitations are not signed agreements or qualified products.

Alongside the existing DRI portable-extension release, publish separate CP/M application, FlexiBUS peripheral and optional Logix display compatibility profiles, reference-driver and test access, non-exclusive implementation principles and support-roadmap requirements. Exact fees and support duration remain to be settled.

Invite computer, software and peripheral suppliers to test named configurations and document failures before public demonstrations. Supplier attendance and passing results must be verified; no announcement of an unsigned OEM.

Present a 50-minute cross-vendor campaign before questions. Demonstrate applications/documents, then independent BPI, FlexiBUS, Apple native drivers and optional video. BPI management speaks with partners. State that the next generation breaks native Z80 binary compatibility; C source/API portability reduces migration work and a planned optional Z80 compatibility coprocessor supports qualified legacy software. Reveal neither processor word size nor architecture before NCC 1980. See ncc_1979_campaign.json.

Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Teach documented APIs, file interchange, C portability boundaries and device-class drivers. Publish a directory distinguishing shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.

Promote the separately recorded Tandy customer release and only individually qualified SMC or peripheral products. Update directory evidence; do not imply all licensed chips, every peripheral class or new independent OEM systems are shipping.

Target Tandy shipping, one additional named OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension/FlexiBUS option, another OEM in qualification, dealer/integrator configurations and third-party devices in several categories. These are adoption targets, not recorded achievements or contracted orders.

Publish verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Target three to five non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations by NCC 1980, counting Tandy once and excluding duplicate dealer builds. Do not disclose the new processor architecture early.

stages.description: Explain customer investment and independent choices for software, peripherals and displays.
Run supported application workflows on Aurelia and the Model II prototype. Use separately qualified host editions; preserve documents and supported semantics without promising identical binaries.
Demonstrate Abacus first, then independent BPI business records and summary export. BPI remains an independent licensor; no BPI Model II port is implied.
Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Identification, driver support and application features are separately verified. Attach only at quiescent ports.
Show native Apple II drivers and optional display cards separately. No Apple CP/M/Z80 execution or automatic adaptation of existing Apple graphics is implied.

DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, BPI management and confirmed peripheral participants explain responsibilities and commercial access. No prospective OEM is presented as signed. SMC is a future qualified source, not June production supply.

Adam states that the next generation will break native Z80 binary compatibility. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration effort; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. A planned optional Z80 coprocessor offers qualified legacy execution. Architecture and word size remain secret until NCC 1980. Eight-bit systems retain business uses and broaden into homes and education as prices fall. Adam forecasts that next-generation computers using an existing television and basic storage will remain above roughly $100 for about a decade; this is a strategic expectation, not a withdrawal date or price guarantee.
Separate shipping products, prototypes, future plans and adoption targets; provide documented configurations, licence terms, directory and developer-registration contacts.

premiere.venue: Booked presentation space; main-stage access, exact slot and AV qualification remain to be confirmed.
demonstration_protocol: Aurelia-to-Model-II Abacus document round trip using qualified host editions and supported common features
Test actual transfer route and floppy/file formats; do not imply identical disk media support
Mark Model II as prototype until October customer release
Publish RAM, TPA, load/recalculation and document-capacity limits; no undocumented hardware access guarantee
Label prepared data and recordings; preserve independent BPI branding and partner clearances

migration.disclosure: Public 1979 materials withhold word size, ISA details and architecture; full project technical catalog is an author-facing specification, not a 1979 press kit.
migration.source_path: Use the existing Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separated platform adapters. Recompile for the later target; review assembly, integer/pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access.
migration.legacy_path: Planned optional Z80 coprocessor for qualified legacy applications. Implementation details remain confidential; this is not a universal guarantee for hardware-dependent software.
migration.public_status: Future commitment, not a shipping or fully qualified June-1979 product.
migration.support: Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development; publish a funded duration before making a dated service guarantee.

eight_bit_outlook.status: Adam strategic forecast, not an engineering or economic guarantee.
eight_bit_outlook.trajectory: Continue useful business installations while declining costs broaden home, education and personal use; no fixed date when all business users switch.
eight_bit_outlook.price_basis: Nominal future US retail dollars before tax for a next-generation computer using an existing television and basic storage; screen and complete disk/printer business configuration excluded. Exact basic-storage inclusion remains to be defined.
eight_bit_outlook.interpretation: Adam does not expect the threshold within roughly a decade. This is not a discontinuation date, promise of each model remaining in production or automatic retirement when the threshold is crossed.
eight_bit_outlook.engineering_gap: Current professional digital monitor interface does not provide consumer-TV output; a later TV-capable configuration would need separate engineering and costing.

existing_anchors.Tandy: Existing agreement: CP/M, native display adapter, FlexiBUS option and Abacus; no video requirement or BPI port.
existing_anchors.Apple: Existing native expansion cooperation and peripheral/display demonstrations; no Z80 or CP/M execution provided.

peripheral_programme.opportunity: Wide carriage, letter quality, specialist forms and faster devices
peripheral_programme.requirement: Status, character/graphics, paper and form controls; existing basic printer protocol is insufficient for every feature.
New plotting profile and application support required.
Serial data, flow control, modem status/control profile and drivers required.

peripheral_programme.opportunity: Larger floppies, backup and selected hard disks
peripheral_programme.requirement: Geometry, removable-media errors, durable flush, boot rules and measured throughput; native faster controllers remain legitimate.
Published class/vendor extension profile and host drivers; no auto-executing foreign-ISA ROM drivers.

end_1979.peripheral_categories: Several, only counted after verified shipping
end_1979.status: Target, not an achieved market outcome.

ncc1980.counting: Count Tandy once; count distinct OEMs with official supported configurations, not multiple dealer builds or product SKUs.
ncc1980.status: Target, not signed contracts or actual deliveries.

metrics: Independent OEM configurations and qualified application editions
Compatible computer sell-through by all vendors
Third-party peripheral shipments and supported device classes

evidence.scope: December 1979 primary manual supports North Star CP/M integration precedent, not an actual alternate partnership.
May 1979 reproduced Vector price list supports existing CP/M and display investment.
Period advertising supports Cromemco independent OS/compatibility positioning.
Later primary manual; architecture precedent only, not proof of June 1979 adapter availability.

disclosure_policy.scope: Every 1979 keynote, Q&A, press release, advertisement, dealer script, sales proposal, partner/OEM briefing, roadshow, developer clinic and demonstration. Confidential internal engineering is not a public announcement.
permitted: Native binary compatibility with existing Z80 applications will break.
The established C development environment and documented interfaces will minimise source migration effort; adaptation, recompilation and testing remain necessary.
An optional Z80 coprocessor is planned for qualified legacy applications; availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model.
Eight-bit systems retain years of business use and increasingly serve homes and education; the next-generation sub-$100 forecast is roughly a decade away, not a withdrawal deadline.
withheld: Future product, processor and operating-system names.
Word size, instruction set, register model, execution design, address width, memory organisation and protection.
Clock rates, performance claims, chip counts, schematics, board photographs, bus topology and future display specifications.
Coprocessor implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration.
Future-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries, benchmarks and demonstrations that allow architectural inference.
disclosure_policy.enforcement: Use only released 8-bit products in 1979 demonstrations and clinics. Review slides, screenshots, captions, attachments and linked specifications as well as speech. Do not attach the all-years technical catalog or disclose future implementation details to prospective partners; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional video specifications remain available.
disclosure_policy.qa_response: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

costs: OEM engineering kits and port assistance
Workshops, conformance engineering and directory maintenance
Venue, AV, demonstrations and rights-cleared recordings
Dealer roadshows, trade press and joint advertising
Developer migration clinics and ongoing CP/M support
economics.treatment: Operating programme expenditure, not unit hardware BOM. No fabricated zero budget or assumed OEM sales receipts. BPI, Tandy and independent suppliers account for their own receipts.
economics.forecast_cutoff: The original forecast through May 31, 1979 remains unchanged. sales_forecast.json separately extends demand and delivery projections through November 30 with explicit June pricing, campaign effects, substitution and capacity assumptions. No effects are applied retroactively; OEM adoption targets are not shipments. A separate COMDEX-to-NCC 1980 extension now reaches May 18 with product-specific demand and Academy capacity; prior period forecasts are unchanged.

ncc_1980_campaign.title: Artemis. A new generation. A familiar way to work.
ncc_1980_campaign.status: Accepted campaign plan; demonstrations and performance claims require validation

compatibility_policy.scope: Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path.
compatibility_policy.exclusions: Undocumented hardware access, unqualified peripherals and unsupported interfaces; no promise of unchanged speed, unlimited memory, or every future device. Z80 programs use their separately qualified compatibility path.
compatibility_policy.delivery_requirements: Publish versioned ABI/API eligibility and conformance tests; preserve reference binaries and regression workloads; budget compatibility engineering, runtime distribution and support. Staffing, funding and validation remain explicit launch readiness gates.
compatibility_policy.status: Official scenario commitment at NCC 1980; future fulfilment is not established evidence.

presentation.content: Adam: the business task and familiar way to work
AIONix multitasking: edit, calculate and switch using familiar TUI conventions
Native Business Tools and Abacus 2 charts/document fields; then independent BPI head demonstrates accounting
One maintained C project, separate ERA and Z80 builds; optional compatibility card runs qualified unchanged legacy binaries
Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis: verified calculation benchmark, then visible animation
Reveal: 32-bit RISC ERA 1 developed by AION
Publish the compatibility commitment through 2000 and its precise scope
Partners: independent BPI head, Digital Research and qualified device/software partners
Prices, qualified configurations, order routes, developer kits and training

claims.memory: Beyond the 64 KB application barrier; demonstrate a measured resident workload on a named 128 KB or 256 KB configuration. Finite RAM and process limits remain; no demand paging promised.
claims.os: Professional multitasking AIONix with Unix V7-inspired behaviour and familiar Logix TUI/keyboard conventions. Do not claim a Unix source licence or trademark endorsement without an established agreement.
claims.compiler: Artemis-hosted AION C IDE supplies ERA native and Z80 cross-compilers, target libraries and separate executables. Portable code following guidelines can require small changes; quantify changes for each demonstration rather than promising zero work.
claims.applications: Native Abacus 2, Business Tools and qualified independent BPI editions. Pulse 1 remains Aurelia+ software; a card demonstration requires guest OS/memory qualification. Native Pulse 3 and Abacus 3 launch only at COMDEX on November 19.
claims.continuity: Aurelia+ remains a supported value option; compatible independent 8-bit computers grow the ecosystem. No forced migration or promise that cheaper 8-bit demand disappears.

benchmark.compute: Identical vector transformations and fixed-point precision, inputs, rounding and verified output; time computation separately from rendering and I/O. Publish source, compiler options, configuration and repeat-run range.
benchmark.visual: Same shaded rotating cube, geometry and image quality; identify display hardware, frame-buffer and display-transfer costs separately. Do not infer pure CPU speed from unequal graphics systems.
benchmark.claim_gate: Publish measured ratios only after reproducible qualification; no forecast assumes an unmeasured speed multiplier.

activities.action: Private partner qualification, dealer rehearsal, porting clinic pilots and embargoed briefings; public teaser promises a familiar workflow without revealing architecture or word size.
Live 55-minute keynote, independent BPI appearance after Abacus, benchmark method/results if measured, compatibility policy, software/configuration matrix and ordering sheets.
Dealer demonstrations and customer workflow trials; press technical briefing; Academy transition classes and developer migration clinics; maintain issue/qualification register.

Regional dealer roadshows, independent developer/OEM certification workshops, customer case studies with consent and measured results; review conversion, delivery backlog, porting effort and support capacity monthly.
Demonstrate released Abacus 3 and Pulse 3 on Artemis, report compatibility progress and retain Aurelia maintenance messaging. No pre-release revenue in the November 18 forecast.

launch_gates: Measured benchmark and reproducible display comparison
Qualified demo memory/process footprint and printing paths
Published native/card application matrix and OS licensing status
Versioned compatibility policy, engineering owner, staffing and funded maintenance plan
Dealer stock/service readiness and Academy instructor qualification
ncc_1980_campaign.sales_measurement: Track qualified leads, demonstrations, orders, deliveries, cancellations, model substitution, porting effort, application attachments and service issues separately. Campaign budget and measured conversion rates remain open inputs.

mono_pro_campaign.scope: Incremental qualified 80×40 and 80×25 high-resolution text demonstrations, grayscale bitmap/sprites, explicit old-monitor limitations and replaceable card. Retain existing presentation duration; incorporate into Artemis product demonstration.
mono_pro_campaign.measurement: Track dealer enquiries and conversions by monitor bundle. 6/12/18% assumed Artemis intent uplift combines display appeal and this campaign; not an empirical ROI claim.

ncc_1980_campaign.artemis_configuration_policy: Artemis 128: 16 KiB card with Mono II or Color II. Artemis 256: 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips and 32 KiB card with Mono Pro or Color II. Mono Pro requires the professional card; Color II uses legacy timings. See artemis_tiers.json.

metadata.title: COMDEX 1979 campaign and presentation
metadata.status: Accepted alternative-history campaign; demonstrations require qualification, not claimed measured results

messages.campaign: More room to work. More freedom to choose.
messages.abacus_2: Calculate once. Chart it. Print the documents.

stages.description: Adam: growing businesses need more capacity, less waiting and compatible choices.
Identical live calculated shaded-cube animation on Aurelia and Aurelia+, followed by identical Abacus recalculation and chart generation; present measured results.
Chart employee pay values; link fields to a payslip layout; preview employees and print the entire batch.
The head of independent BPI demonstrates BPI Payroll as the source of calculated values, documented file exchange and reconciled totals.
Demonstrate a focused information-management task using tested, implemented capabilities; no implied live cross-application integration.
Introduce the Compatibility Kit, reference adapters and diagnostics. Show an independent application implementation only after qualification; otherwise show clearly labelled engineering work.
BPI leadership joins participating peripheral/computer suppliers. Name products and distinguish shipping, qualified and prototype status.
Purchasing, existing-Aurelia upgrades, ongoing support and independent manufacturer participation; new hardware focus on Aurelia+.

speed_demonstration.workload: Calculate rotation, project vertices, determine visible faces, calculate shading and draw a fixed sequence of cube rotations live. No prerecorded animation or precomputed frames.
controls: Same executable and inputs on both machines, compatible with both
Same resolution, shading method, rendering settings and equivalent qualified display configurations; disclose unavoidable differences
Visible start countdown, elapsed time and completed-frame count
Fixed frame/rotation sequence completes the same amount of work; no silent frame skipping or quality reduction
Use a workload that fits both machines; demonstrate additional capacity separately
Both machines must finish correctly; publish results only after measurement
speed_demonstration.business_comparison: Same Abacus 2.0 executable, worksheet values/formulas, calculation settings and chart workload. Compare recalculation and chart-generation time; exclude physical printer time.
speed_demonstration.interpretation: Animation measures the combined calculation/display path, not pure CPU performance. The catalog clocks are 4 and 6 MHz, but no 1.5x or other application speedup is promised.

headline_features: Document layouts populated by spreadsheet field values
abacus_demonstration.chart_scope: Use the catalogued text-mode vertical or horizontal bar charts; do not imply unimplemented graphical chart types.
abacus_demonstration.data: Fictitious employees with names, departments, pay components, deductions and precalculated net pay; one row per employee.
steps: Inspect precalculated values and reconcile totals
Show a payroll-cost bar chart by department
Open one reusable payslip layout and identify linked spreadsheet fields
Preview different employees to show field substitution
Print one complete payslip per employee from the same layout
acceptance: Validate field mapping, missing values, numeric formatting and rounding
Validate pagination and ensure every selected employee prints exactly once with the correct values
Validate save/reopen and preserve spreadsheet/document contents
Reconcile BPI-exported values with source totals through documented versioned disk-file exchange
abacus_demonstration.boundary: Abacus charts, formats and prints supplied calculations. Payroll law/rules, statutory deductions and updates belong to the payroll application or properly maintained worksheet. No direct ledger write-back or live database link.
abacus_demonstration.sparse_storage: Supporting implementation advantage for useful workloads, not a permanently exclusive general technique.
abacus_demonstration.existing_owners: Promote Abacus 2.0 on both Aurelia and Aurelia+ in supported configurations. Do not imply a new computer is required.

partner_policy.bpi: Independent branding, management, licences and support. The head of BPI speaks immediately after Abacus and joins the partner segment.
partner_policy.peripherals: Demonstrate only individually qualified configurations. Invitations and targets are not agreements or shipments.
partner_policy.manufacturers: Published interfaces and kit permit independent Aurelia-class implementations; support and certification optional. Native hardware adapters are valid; FlexiBUS and Logix video are separate profiles. Proper application/OS/firmware licences remain necessary.

activities.activity: Confidential dealer/BPI training, demo qualification, workflow rehearsal and press-material preparation. Invite business buyers and manufacturers to separate sessions; do not disclose unreleased specifications or pricing publicly.

Trade-press demos and advertisements show side-by-side speed, charts and printed payslips. Press pack includes sample data/layouts, configurations and measured results. Paid broadcasting/celebrity promotion requires confirmed arrangements.
Business-workflow stations, existing-owner upgrade consultations, peripheral demos and manufacturer clinics. Each visitor gets a relevant next step.
Dealer roadshows and Academy sessions: From spreadsheet to finished documents. Follow up with demonstrations and quotations.
Manufacturer porting workshops and publication of verified configuration-specific compatibility results.

commercial_policy.new_buyers: Clearly price hardware, required software and printing configuration; separately quote BPI licences and specialist setup.
commercial_policy.existing_owners: New capabilities for the computer you already own. Publish configuration requirements and explain workloads that benefit from Aurelia+.
commercial_policy.manufacturers: Freely accessible specifications/self-tests, modest physical-kit pricing, optional bounded assistance and configuration-specific certification; no exclusive partnership required.
commercial_policy.suppliers: Interoperability sessions and verified directory listings; document production supplies a concrete printer use case.
commercial_policy.promotion: Prefer training, demonstration access and implementation help over another general price cut. Discounts, contracts and media spend are not invented.

comdex_1979_campaign.strategy: Logix focuses new hardware development and promotion on Aurelia+ while enabling independent Aurelia-class clones and maintaining installed-base support; no immediate withdrawal date.

disclosure.permitted: Native binary compatibility will change; established C practices reduce migration work; a planned optional Z80 path supports qualified legacy code.
disclosure.withheld: No future product/processor/OS names, word size, architecture, future-target compiler output, binaries or revealing demonstrations before NCC 1980.

business: Delivered Aurelia+ systems and lead times
ecosystem: Applications qualified on named independent computers
metrics.counting: Track delivery and ecosystem progress separately. Kit registrations, prototypes, applications and certification submissions are not computer sales.

economics.status: Campaign, venue/AV, staffing, demo equipment, printing, press, travel and workshop budgets remain to be approved; no ROI claim.
economics.forecast_boundary: Original November 30 forecasts remain unchanged, with no separate confidential-preparation uplift. sales_forecast.json now contains a distinct December–May 18 extension with explicit campaign, price-premium, substitution and capacity assumptions; no campaign delivery guarantee.

comdex_1982_campaign.status: Proposed marketing campaign accompanying the accepted November offering. Headline, budget and commercial claims remain subject to final joint review.

messages.proof: Native 800x600 drawing area on the 17-inch screen, four shades selected from 16 levels, static CAD palette and demonstrated line quality.

messages.message: Keep commands and drawing in view
messages.proof: Colour command/status display alongside the dedicated drawing screen, with explicit keyboard/mouse focus.

messages.message: Take the drawing beyond the screen
messages.proof: Save, reopen, exchange and plot the same test drawing; verify coordinates and output scale.

messages.message: Buy an application with a supported platform
messages.proof: Autodesk application support and Logix hardware/integration support, qualified configurations, dealer training and a clear upgrade route.

script.action: Open a representative mechanical or floor-plan drawing from disk; show the command screen and drawing screen together.
Create and edit supported lines/arcs using typed coordinates and mouse input. Use only commands present in the qualified AutoCAD 1.0 build.
Pan/zoom and compare ordinary versus antialiased line rendering at the same scale. State measured redraw behaviour; do not promise arbitrary real-time performance.
Save and reopen the drawing, demonstrate tested exchange, and show the resulting plot.
Explain complete-system and existing-owner upgrade routes, support ownership, and book an evaluation.

hero_demo.plotter_timing: Run a small live plot; disclose any larger pre-plotted sample as such. Do not imply a long plot completes within a short demonstration.
hero_demo.proof_policy: Use a fixed published test drawing and configuration. Distinguish line-rendering smoothness from numerical geometry accuracy; no unsupported competitor speed comparison.

ncc_1982_campaign.title: NCC 1982 — Pointy ideas with a solid point.
ncc_1982_campaign.headline: Pointy ideas with a solid point.
ncc_1982_campaign.subheadline: Introducing the Logix Mouse. Point, select, and get to work.
ncc_1982_campaign.status: Accepted alternative-history offering and planned campaign; budgets are planning provisions, not observed spending.
messages: Point directly to your work: keyboard and mouse work together.
See more in your information: colour Abacus reports and professional drawings.
Choose a platform that grows with you: upgrades, independent software and compatible manufacturers.
ncc_1982_campaign.availability: June colour/mouse offering and around-June professional hardware availability. AutoCAD is a November COMDEX development target, not a June shipping application.
ncc_1982_campaign.software_update_policy: CP/M and AIONix TUI mouse updates carry no new licence fee for existing licensed users; fulfillment media ships with mouse/upgrade kits (costed in mouse pack). Standalone replacement media and installation are quoted separately. Replaceable TUI services can update existing binaries; static libraries require relinking, custom drawing requires adaptation.
presentation: Open a familiar Abacus worksheet and edit with keyboard.
Use the mouse to select a field, activate a button and scroll with both rollers.
Show a colour report with labels/patterns preserving monochrome meaning.
Demonstrate a supported older application and explain its exact update path.
Show the colour upgrade for an existing compatible Artemis.
Close with qualified 800x600 professional graphics and the Autodesk November target.

No invented fixed-price complete-system SKU.
ncc_1982_campaign.developer_program: Demonstrate task -> branch -> discussion -> target build -> test -> labelled release. Promote $745.23 Team Edition with clear one-server/four-concurrent-user entitlement; hardware separate. Offer scheduled porting clinics and documented compatibility testing.
ncc_1982_campaign.autodesk_claim: Autodesk is developing AutoCAD for Artemis with a complete Logix-funded development environment; joint November COMDEX presentation is the target. Show an early Autodesk build only if approved and stable, labelled development software.

team_development_program.claim_policy: Robustness is a design goal demonstrated by recovery and reproducible builds, not an untested most-robust comparison. No write-once/run-anywhere or Apple/Commodore launch claim.
